headline: Ishraque Hossain to announce resignation as state minister today
summary: The State Minister for Liberation War Affairs arrives at the National Press Club to officially step down from his post.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain arrived at the National Press Club on Monday afternoon to announce his resignation from the post.
In a verified Facebook post, he stated that he would make the final announcement and face journalists at 2:00 PM.
Hossain expressed his intention to work with even greater enthusiasm as a BNP worker to fight against drugs in the country.
He mentioned that he would focus on strengthening the organizational power of the Generation Party (Projonmo Dal) through various district visits.
The minister also criticized some 'civilized people' on Facebook who were celebrating his departure, urging them to join future movements from abroad if needed.
He concluded his announcement by emphasizing that his priority is now the eradication of drugs over holding a ministerial position.
caption:
From state minister to drug-war activist. Ishraque Hossain is stepping down today.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain arrived at the National Press Club on Monday afternoon to announce his resignation from the post.

In a verified Facebook post, he stated that he would make the final announcement and face journalists at 2:00 PM.

Hossain expressed his intention to work with even greater enthusiasm as a BNP worker to fight against drugs in the country.

He mentioned that he would focus on strengthening the organizational power of the Generation Party (Projonmo Dal) through various district visits.

The minister also criticized some 'civilized people' on Facebook who were celebrating his departure, urging them to join future movements from abroad if needed.

He concluded his announcement by emphasizing that his priority is now the eradication of drugs over holding a ministerial position.

headline_marked: PM [[inaugurates July Memorial]] and renovated Osmani Udyan
headline: PM inaugurates July Memorial and renovated Osmani Udyan
summary: The 90-foot-high memorial honors 834 martyrs of the 2024 July Uprising, featuring relief sculptures of Bangladesh's struggle for freedom.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the July Memorial at Osmani Udyan in Dhaka on Monday morning. The event was attended by family members of those killed in the July Uprising, including the fathers of Abu Sayed and Mir Mahfuzur Rahman Mugdho.

The 90-foot-high July Memorial is dedicated to preserving the memory of the martyrs of the 2024 July Uprising. It spans nearly one acre and lists the names of 834 martyrs, engraved using laser-cutting technology, with 20 symbolic tombstones installed in front.

The memorial features extensive relief sculptures depicting the history of Bangladesh's movements, including the 1952 Language Movement, the 1969 Mass Uprising, the 1971 Liberation War, the 1990 Mass Movement, and the 2024 July Uprising.

Alongside the memorial, the Prime Minister also opened the modernised Osmani Udyan. The 23-acre park, located at the junction of Old and New Dhaka, has been transformed into a green, safe recreational space for city residents.

The park's renovation includes the restoration of an old waterbody and the creation of five new ones, along with 3.1 kilometres of walking trails, a gymnasium, and a rainwater harvesting system with a 50,000-litre capacity.
The ceremony was attended by high-ranking officials, including Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and the administrators of the Dhaka South and North City Corporations.
Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister planted a sapling on the memorial premises and toured the park's new library.
caption:
